questions.question_text:
A flow network is recorded in this table.
$\begin{array}{c|ccccc} \text{From / To} & D & E & F & G & H \\ \hline D & - & 6 & - & - & 8 \\ E & - & - & - & - & - \\ F & 12 & - & - & 19 & - \\ G & - & - & - & - & 14 \\ H & - & 22 & - & - & - \end{array}$
Which vertex is the source and which is the sink?

options.text: $F$ is the source and $E$ is the sink
$D$ is the source and $E$ is the sink
options.why: Took the first row heading as the source; column $D$ contains a $12$, so an edge is directed into $D$ and it cannot be the source.

options.text: $F$ is the source and $H$ is the sink
options.why: Chose the sink as the vertex that the most edges point into ($D$ and $G$ both reach $H$), but row $H$ contains a $22$, so an edge still leaves $H$.

options.text: $D$ is the source and $H$ is the sink
options.why: Made both slips at once: read the first row heading as the source and the most-pointed-to vertex as the sink, checking neither column $D$ nor row $H$ for entries.

questions.solution_text:
Column $F$ contains only dashes, so no edge is directed into $F$.
Row $E$ contains only dashes, so no edge is directed out of $E$.
$F$ is the source and $E$ is the sink.

options.why: Included the $20$ from edge $S \to A$, but that edge leaves $S$, so it belongs in row $S$, column $A$.
Recorded only one of the two edges leaving $A$, missing the edge $A \to D$ of capacity $11$.
Read down column $A$ instead of across row $A$, recording the edge that enters $A$ rather than those that leave it.

questions.solution_text:
Row $A$ records only the edges directed away from $A$.
These are $A \to C$ ($13$) and $A \to D$ ($11$).
$\begin{array}{c|cccccc} \text{From / To} & S & A & B & C & D & T \\ \hline A & - & - & - & 13 & 11 & - \end{array}$

options.why: The $3$ sits in row $P$, column $Q$, so that edge runs from $P$ to $Q$; drawing $B$ reverses it by reading the column as the starting vertex.
The $5$ is in row $S$, column $P$ and the $7$ in row $S$, column $Q$; drawing $C$ swaps the two capacities leaving $S$.
The $4$ sits in row $Q$, column $T$, so it runs from $Q$ to $T$; drawing $D$ reverses it, which would also leave an edge directed out of the sink.

questions.solution_text:
Row $S$ gives $S \to P$ ($5$) and $S \to Q$ ($7$).
Row $P$ gives $P \to Q$ ($3$) and $P \to T$ ($6$).
Row $Q$ gives $Q \to T$ ($4$).
Drawing $A$ matches every row of the table.

options.why: The $9$ sits in row $A$, column $C$, so $A \to C$ is drawn correctly; this option reads the column heading as the starting vertex.
Row $B$ has a $17$ in column $T$ and the diagram does draw $B \to T$ with $17$; this option counts the edges of the diagram without checking the row headings.

options.why: Row $B$ has only one entry, in column $T$, so no edge runs from $B$ to $C$; this option assumes every middle vertex must connect to every other.

questions.solution_text:
Row $S$ gives $S \to A$ with capacity $14$ and $S \to B$ with capacity $26$.
The diagram labels $SA$ as $26$ and $SB$ as $14$.
The two capacities leaving $S$ have been swapped; $SA$ should be $14$ and $SB$ should be $26$.

questions.question_text:
A mine sends ore along one-way conveyors, with capacities in tonnes per hour: $M$ to $R$ ($120$), $M$ to $N$ ($95$), $R$ to $K$ ($60$), $N$ to $K$ ($80$), $N$ to $H$ ($45$), and $K$ to $H$ ($130$).
In the flow network described, which vertex is the sink?

options.why: $K$ receives ore from two conveyors, but ore still leaves $K$ for $H$, so $K$ is not where the network ends.
Named the vertex that nothing is directed into, which identifies the source rather than the sink.
Chose a middle vertex; two conveyors leave $N$, so it cannot be the sink.

questions.question_text:
A flow network with six vertices is recorded in this table.
$\begin{array}{c|cccccc} \text{From / To} & A & B & C & D & E & F \\ \hline A & - & 18 & - & - & - & - \\ B & - & - & - & - & 40 & - \\ C & - & 22 & - & - & - & 15 \\ D & 31 & - & 27 & - & - & - \\ E & - & - & - & - & - & - \\ F & - & - & - & - & 12 & - \end{array}$
Which vertex is the source?

options.why: Took the first row heading, but column $A$ contains a $31$, so an edge is directed into $A$.
Chose the vertex with the empty row, which identifies the sink; the source has the empty column.
Chose a vertex with two edges leaving it, but column $C$ contains a $27$, so an edge is directed into $C$.

questions.solution_text:
The source has no edge directed into it, so its column is entirely dashes.
Column $D$ contains only dashes.
$D$ is the source.

options.why: Included the $35$ from edge $G \to J$, which leaves $G$ and so belongs in row $G$, column $J$.
Read down column $J$ instead of across row $J$, recording the edge that enters $J$ rather than those leaving it.
Put the $21$ in column $L$ instead of column $M$; the edge $J \to M$ ends at $M$, and it is $M \to L$ that reaches $L$.

questions.solution_text:
Row $J$ records only the edges directed away from $J$.
These are $J \to K$ ($9$) and $J \to M$ ($21$).
$\begin{array}{c|cccccc} \text{From / To} & G & H & J & K & L & M \\ \hline J & - & - & - & 9 & - & 21 \end{array}$

questions.question_text:
A flow network is recorded in this table.
$\begin{array}{c|cccccc} \text{From / To} & S & A & B & C & D & T \\ \hline S & - & 33 & 29 & - & - & - \\ A & - & - & - & 14 & 12 & - \\ B & - & - & - & - & 25 & - \\ C & - & - & - & - & - & 18 \\ D & - & - & - & - & - & 41 \\ T & - & - & - & - & - & - \end{array}$
Which of these edges does **not** appear in the network drawn from this table?

options.why: This edge does appear: the $12$ sits in row $A$, column $D$.
This edge does appear: the $18$ sits in row $C$, column $T$.
This edge does appear: the $29$ sits in row $S$, column $B$.

questions.solution_text:
Row $B$ has just one entry, a $25$ in column $D$.
So the $25$ edge runs from $B$ to $D$, and column $C$ in row $B$ is a dash.
There is no edge from $B$ to $C$.
